text:
alyssa: heads up — after the kernel-routing change yesterday I'm seeing a spike in OOMs and much higher fragmentation on our p3-like fleet. not just bigger peak, more small free holes that don't get reused.

jordan: timeline? which commit/rollout?

alyssa: rolled at 09:12 UTC (routing v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0). first OOMs ~09:18. repro on canary: 1/10 runs OOM for chat-8k workloads.

sam_w: can you paste the allocator stats snapshot? even a diff helps.

alyssa: pasted below — this is from our debug dump after a repro run:

```
AllocState: total_gpu=31.9GB, used=28.4GB, free=3.5GB
slab_map: 64B: 120k allocs, 4MB free fragments
         4KB: 30k allocs, 1.2GB free fragments
         1MB: 2k allocs, 200MB free fragments
workspace: reserved=2GB, live=1.1GB
kv_cache: caches=540MB active, 1.6GB cold segments
fragmentation_ratio: 0.42
last_gc: reclaimed 60MB
gc_runs_since_boot: 7
```

alyssa: current knobs: expandable_segments=true, max_split_size_mb=64, garbage_collection_threshold=0.25

nina: kv cache warmup is doing lots of small allocations — when sequences grow we append small tensors into workspace which causes many 4KB/64B churns. that plus the routing change increased kernel concurrency, so allocator gets more interleaved small frees. :thinking:

sam_w: that fragmentation_ratio (0.42) + only 60MB reclaimed suggests GC threshold is too aggressive (not running often enough) or split-size too small so we can't coalesce. could try bumping max_split_size_mb to 128 and lowering garbage_collection_threshold to 0.15 as an A/B. also try temporary expandable_segments=false to force larger contiguous segments.

jordan: agree. quick experiment matrix:
- baseline (current knobs)
- max_split_size_mb=128
- expandable_segments=false
- garbage_collection_threshold=0.15
- combo: max_split_size_mb=128 + gc=0.15

matt_r: i'll run the canary harness across 10 runs per config on the canary pool. use this command: 

```bash
./tools/bench_infer.sh --model chat-8k --runs 10 --knobs "max_split_size_mb=128,garbage_collection_threshold=0.15"
```

matt_r: also add `--trace-malloc` to collect the small-allocation histogram.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout v2.5.0 -> 30% at 09:10 UTC by @deploy-bot

alyssa: i have a perf flame — after routing change we get many more kernel_... calls at short durations, lots of tiny allocations between kernels. sending pprof link: http://pprof.internal/redwood/pprof?run=2632145678

sam_w: saw similar in past: kernel scheduling bumps concurrency causing allocator to interleave tiny allocs; if segments are expandable we tend to split slabs more often which increases fragmentation. one mitigation is to favor buffer reuse: when releasing temporary tensors, return to a small-object pool instead of free. cheap to implement: keep a free-list keyed by shape/size class.

nina: note: KV cache warmup will still trample the pool if we allocate many unique sizes. recommend a two-tier: small-size freelist + coalescing GC that runs after warmup windows.

jordan: is there an observable latency/regression risk if we run GC more frequently?

sam_w: yes, GC costs CPU/GPU sync. lowering threshold to 0.15 will run GC earlier but should reclaim bigger contiguous runs and reduce failed mallocs. tradeoff: brief stalls vs fewer OOMs. we should measure p99 latency with the harness.

alyssa: initial quick test on my laptop (A100 node) — changed max_split_size_mb to 128 and gc to 0.15: 10/10 runs successful, fragmentation dropped to 0.28, p99 request time +30ms on average.

matt_r: good signal. let's run 3-hour canary to check long-tail. i'm kicking off jobs now.

infra-bot: job: canary-run-2632145980 started by matt_r

jordan: if canary is good, plan for gradual rollout and enable a fallback: if OOM spikes > threshold revert routing to v2.4.1 automatically.

alyssa: also captured a CUDA OOM log — shows failed allocation 134217728 bytes (128MB) while free=110MB. that's exactly hitting split boundary. we should make max_split_size_mb >= largest KV segment we allocate during warmup.

sam_w: good catch. consider an instrumentation: track largest single allocation size per request and log histograms; then set max_split_size_mb to cover 95th percentile.

nina: noted. i'll add instrumentation to kv-warmup path to record largest alloc size (simple atomic max).

matt_r: after canary completes i'll post results here. if green, we'll roll config change cluster-wide and keep routing change.

alyssa: thanks everyone — appreciate the quick triage. will follow up with the pprof + histograms once canary finishes. :thumbsup:
